finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to 0.01, or use a negative price or qty, to pay an arbitrary or negative amount, or to get a credit or refund. The legitimate /checkout-v2 endpoint looks prices up server-side, but this older route stays reachable.

trace.note: POST /checkout handler accepts the request body
total = sum(i.price * i.qty) using unvalidated client values
total is passed directly to the payment charge
charged amount is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: There is no server-side price lookup, no type, range or sign validation on price or qty, no check that total > 0, and no catalog verification. Only req.user.id is used, and no authentication middleware is visible in this file. The /checkout-v2 route shows the catalog lookup is available but is not applied here.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup or sign/type/range check and cart.js:6 charges that total, unlike the guarded /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14); any user who can reach the route (likely a low-privilege authenticated one, since req.user.id is used) can set the price.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not validate qty or the catalog price. A non-numeric qty (e.g. a string such as "abc", NaN or a non-finite value) makes Math.floor return NaN, and Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN, so the total becomes NaN. Infinity passes through as Infinity. An unknown sku can make the price undefined, which also gives NaN. The result is an invalid charge amount that can bypass payment, depending on how payments.charge handles NaN. There is also no upper bound on qty or on the number of items, so a huge items array causes a serial catalog lookup per item (resource abuse). This is lower confidence than F1 because it depends on the behavior of charge().

trace.note: iterates attacker-supplied items with no length limit or Array check
catalog price for the attacker-chosen sku; the result is not checked for undefined
Math.max(1, Math.floor(qty)) propagates NaN or Infinity into total
charge is called with the possibly NaN or Infinity total

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, ...) blocks zero and negative qty but not NaN or Infinity. There is no Number.isFinite or Number.isInteger check, no check that the sku exists, no check that total is finite and positive, and no cap on the item count.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js: Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at line 14 only floors non-positive qty, with no isFinite/isInteger check, no sku/price undefined check, no total validation, and no item-count cap. The payments.charge implementation is injected via req and is not in the codebase.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (cart.js:12-16) and unvalidated NaN or Infinity reaches req.payments.charge at cart.js:16 with no guard, but whether that bypasses payment depends on the injected charge() implementation, which isn't available (the only grep hits are the call sites at cart.js:6 and cart.js:16).
